title: Century of Conflict: The Hundred-Years’ War
status: 37 sourced scoped starting references with optional bounded local play
count_note: The supplied tables contain 12 Edwardian, 14 Caroline/interwar and 11 Lancastrian entries: 37 unique dates. All supplied entries are retained.
implementation_rule: Each developed entry is a dated starting-state reference. Later events depend on simulation and player choices. Historical battles, alliances, accessions, deaths and the end of the war are never scheduled merely because they occurred in recorded history.

entries.title: The War Begins
entries.description: Edward III and Philip VI are in open conflict over Aquitaine and contested royal rights.
entries.source_description: Edward III of England and Philip VI of France enter open conflict over French territories and royal authority.

entries.title: The Flemish Alliance
entries.description: Sluys and the unsuccessful siege of Tournai have preceded the September truce at Esplechin.
entries.source_description: Edward III claims the French crown, campaigns with Flemish support, and concludes the Truce of Espléchin in September.

entries.title: The Breton Succession
entries.description: The death of Brittany's duke has opened competing Montfort and Penthièvre–Blois claims; the older John of Montfort has been captured.
entries.source_description: Brittany splits between rival claimants supported by England and France.

entries.title: The Truce of Malestroit
entries.description: The Malestroit truce has interrupted royal campaigning without settling the Breton succession.
entries.source_description: A negotiated suspension of Anglo-French hostilities amid continuing regional tensions.

entries.title: The War Rekindled
entries.description: English operations in Gascony have resumed; Henry of Grosmont's campaign has altered the military situation.
entries.source_description: Major English campaigns resume following the expiry of the truce.

entries.title: Scotland Enters the Campaign
entries.description: Crécy and Neville's Cross have already occurred. David II is a captive; the siege of Calais continues.
entries.source_description: David II invades England in support of France; Edward III campaigns in France.

entries.title: The Truce of Calais
entries.description: Calais has surrendered and a renewed truce follows; occupation and settlement now require administration.
entries.source_description: Calais falls to England and a new Anglo-French truce begins.

entries.title: The Black Prince’s Campaign
entries.description: Edward of Woodstock has conducted a destructive raid from Gascony into southern France.
entries.source_description: Large-scale English offensives resume in southern France.

entries.title: The Captive King
entries.description: John II has been captured at Poitiers. The dauphin Charles must conduct government amid a severe crisis.
entries.source_description: John II of France is captured at Poitiers, creating a French succession and government crisis.

entries.title: The Truces of Bordeaux and Berwick
entries.description: John II remains captive while French government and the Parisian reform movement contest authority.
entries.review_note: Exact diplomatic instruments and the ransom/peace character of the Berwick settlement require dated source review before activation.
entries.source_title: The Truces of Bordeaux and Berwick
entries.source_description: Anglo-French and Anglo-Scottish truces establish separate diplomatic settlements.

entries.title: Edward’s Final Edwardian Offensive
entries.description: Rejected peace terms have been followed by Edward III's new expedition toward Reims.
entries.source_description: Failed peace negotiations lead to a major invasion of France.

entries.title: The Peace of Brétigny
entries.description: Brétigny and the subsequent Calais settlement have established terms for peace and John II's release.
entries.source_description: England and France agree to a major territorial settlement.

entries.title: The Breton Settlement
entries.description: Charles V is king of France. At Auray Charles of Blois has died and the younger John of Montfort has prevailed.
entries.review_note: A 1364 snapshot must not pre-apply the 1365 treaty.
entries.source_description: The Battle of Auray resolves the military contest over Brittany’s succession; the 1365 treaty formalizes its settlement.

entries.title: The Castilian Civil War
entries.description: Henry of Trastámara's intervention has displaced Pedro from much of Castile; the crown remains contested.
entries.source_description: France and England support competing claimants for the Castilian throne.

entries.title: The Caroline War
entries.description: Charles V has renewed the Anglo-French war; Henry of Trastámara has defeated Pedro in Castile.
entries.source_description: Charles V resumes major Anglo-French hostilities; the victorious Trastámara dynasty becomes an important French ally.

entries.title: The Castilian Intervention
entries.description: Castilian naval success at La Rochelle has damaged the English position; the town has returned to French authority.
entries.source_description: Castilian naval power helps France defeat England at La Rochelle.

entries.title: The Portuguese Connection
entries.description: John of Gaunt's long expedition has crossed France without resolving the war.
entries.source_description: Portugal establishes a formal alliance with England while pursuing its own conflict with Castile.

entries.title: The Truce of Bruges
entries.description: French territorial recovery has narrowed England's position and a truce has been negotiated at Bruges.
entries.source_description: Anglo-French hostilities are suspended after extensive French territorial recovery.

entries.title: The War Resumes
entries.description: Edward III has died and Richard II is king; renewed fighting and coastal attacks complicate the transition.
entries.source_description: The truce expires; Edward III dies and Richard II inherits England.

entries.title: The Scottish and Portuguese Fronts
entries.description: A Franco-Scottish expedition has operated against England; Portugal's victory at Aljubarrota has strengthened John I.
entries.source_description: French forces assist Scotland against England; Portugal defeats Castile at Aljubarrota.

entries.title: The Truce of Leulinghem
entries.description: Richard II and Charles VI remain the reigning kings as the Leulinghem truce opens a longer diplomatic interval.
entries.source_description: England, France, and their allies enter a prolonged truce.

entries.title: The Great Diplomatic Settlement
entries.description: Richard II's marriage diplomacy with Isabella of France has reinforced the long truce.
entries.source_description: Anglo-French marriage diplomacy reinforces the long truce.

entries.title: The Lancastrian Accession
entries.description: Henry IV has deposed Richard II and taken the English throne; Richard remains a living captive at this cutoff.
entries.source_description: Henry IV takes the English throne amid deteriorating Anglo-French relations.

entries.title: The Welsh Rebellion
entries.description: Owain Glyndŵr's revolt challenges English rule in Wales while Henry IV seeks to secure his kingship.
entries.source_description: Owain Glyndŵr challenges English rule; France subsequently supports the revolt.

entries.title: The Welsh War and Channel Conflict
entries.description: Henry IV has defeated the Percy rising at Shrewsbury; the Welsh conflict and maritime hostility continue.
entries.review_note: The supplied title is retained as a proposal. Distinguish 1403 activity from the 1404 alliance and the major French expedition of 1405 before activating a snapshot.
entries.source_description: Anglo-French hostility continues through limited operations despite the wider truce arrangements.

entries.title: England and the French Civil War
entries.description: English forces have intervened in support of Burgundian interests in the French civil struggle.
entries.source_title: England and the French Civil War
entries.source_description: English forces intervene in France’s Armagnac–Burgundian struggle.

entries.title: The Lancastrian Invasion
entries.description: Henry V prepares to take his expedition across the Channel. Begin before departure; the campaign’s course and outcomes remain open.
entries.source_description: Henry V invades France; the campaign culminates at Agincourt.

entries.title: The Conquest of Normandy
entries.description: Henry V's renewed expedition has begun a sustained conquest in Normandy; Caen has fallen.
entries.source_description: Henry V launches a sustained campaign to establish English control over Normandy.

entries.title: The Burgundian Alliance
entries.description: Rouen has surrendered and John the Fearless has been killed at Montereau; Philip the Good succeeds in Burgundy.
entries.source_description: The assassination of John the Fearless helps drive Burgundy into an alliance with England.

entries.title: The Treaty of Troyes
entries.description: The Treaty of Troyes designates Henry V as heir and regent while Charles VI remains king; opposition continues.
entries.source_description: Henry V is recognized by the treaty as Charles VI’s successor, but the Dauphin’s supporters continue resisting.

entries.title: The Rival Monarchies
entries.description: Henry V and Charles VI have died. Henry VI is an infant king, while Charles VII maintains a rival French kingship.
entries.source_description: Henry V and Charles VI die; the infant Henry VI and Charles VII become rival claimants.

entries.title: The French Resurgence
entries.description: Orléans has been relieved and Charles VII crowned at Reims; the attempted recovery of Paris has not succeeded.
entries.source_description: The relief of Orléans and the coronation of Charles VII transform French military and political prospects.

entries.title: The Burgundian Reconciliation
entries.description: The Arras settlement has reconciled Philip the Good with Charles VII; Bedford has died.
entries.source_description: Burgundy abandons England and concludes the Treaty of Arras with Charles VII.

entries.title: The Truce of Tours
entries.description: The Tours truce has interrupted major Anglo-French campaigning and marriage negotiations concern Margaret of Anjou.
entries.source_description: England and France suspend major fighting while diplomatic negotiations continue.

entries.title: The Final War
entries.description: The seizure of Fougères has helped break the truce; French and Breton operations have recovered Rouen.
entries.source_description: The truce breaks down; France and Brittany launch the campaign to recover Normandy.

entries.title: The Fall of English Normandy
entries.description: Formigny and the surrender of Cherbourg have completed the collapse of English rule in Normandy.
entries.source_description: French victory at Formigny precedes the completion of Normandy’s reconquest.

entries.title: The Fall of Bordeaux
entries.description: Castillon and the recovery of Bordeaux have ended this historical sequence of major campaigning; Talbot is dead.
entries.review_note: The historical label never imposes a campaign end date or prevents later simulation.
entries.source_description: France recaptures Bordeaux following the Battle of Castillon; the Hundred Years’ War effectively ends.

cutoff_policy: 1415 preserves 11 August before departure; other entries use an explicitly authored 15 December checkpoint after the described developments. No opening hour is invented.
